usage: Commonly used as a verb meaning to take a leisurely walk; it is relaxed and unhurried, not the same as fast walking or exercise walking.
Can be used on its own or with places/time, like after dinner, in the park, or along the harbourfront; it often sounds casual and everyday.
Often combines naturally with verbs of motion or activity in daily speech, especially when talking about going out for a short stroll with family, friends, or a partner.
As a noun, it can refer to the activity of walking for leisure; in conversation, it often carries the idea of a light outdoor pastime rather than serious exercise.
